claim: llm-d's routing layer is built as an implementation of the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension (GIE), which defines InferenceModel/InferencePool CRDs and the Endpoint Picker Protocol, with llm-d introducing its own scheduler implementing the EPP role on top of that contract.
stance_target: the EPP/GIE Endpoint Picker Protocol contract, not kgateway or Istio specifically, is the reusable abstraction boundary a non-k8s backend implementation must satisfy
scope_conditions: kgateway.dev blog, May 20 2025, by Christian Posta (Solo.io)
quoted_support: kgateway provides the perfect foundation for llm-d's intelligent routing through its implementation of the Inference Extension. This extension introduces InferenceModel and InferencePool resources that enable AI-specific routing patterns... llm-d introduces its own scheduler that implements the EPP and brings more powerful selection decisioning.

claim: llm-d's smart routing delivered up to 3x improvement in time-to-first-token and roughly doubled throughput under SLO constraints versus standard load balancing, per the project's own announcement benchmarks.
stance_target: the value proposition of intelligent/inference-aware routing that a customized router should preserve
scope_conditions: llm-d announcement benchmark, cited secondhand by kgateway.dev blog
quoted_support: In benchmark tests, this smart routing delivered up to 3x improvements in time-to-first-token and doubled throughput under SLO constraints.
